Our mission is to foster a modern, stimulating, and inclusive learning experience by empowering the potential of new generations through the responsible use of technology, strengthening their digital skills, and valuing their individual talents.

The company has rapidly evolved as a concrete response to the growing needs of digital education, building a solid bridge between technology and the school environment and enabling continuous training for teachers and students through cutting-edge innovative tools.
Scuolab develops solutions that integrate state-of-the-art technologies — from Virtual Reality to Robotics and Artificial Intelligence — offering accessible and effective resources that make the teaching and learning process more dynamic, immersive, and impactful. Each solution is supported by dedicated training programs that guide educators and learners in seamlessly integrating these technologies into their daily educational activities.
Working in close synergy with the educational community, co-designing solutions with those who experience the classroom every day, Scuolab has already been adopted by more than 80 Italian schools, with over 70,000 platform accesses recorded since its launch.
Our growth is strengthened by collaborations with prestigious institutions recognized for their commitment to education, innovation, and social impact, including Fondazione FOQUS, the educational network Dalla Parte dei Bambini, the National Research Council (CNR), Fondazione Intesa Sanpaolo, and Fondazione Cariplo.

entityDescription:
Introduction to the Faculty of Kinesiology

As the oldest educational and scientific institution in the field of kinesiology in the Republic of Croatia, and
alongside the Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Split and the undergraduate study of Kinesiology at the Faculty of Education of Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek, the Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Zagreb has a long tradition of education and research work, but also a responsibility in promoting kinesiology as a science, quality of class performance and supporting Croatian sport, sports recreation and Physical and Health Education. Through a strong social role, the Faculty of Kinesiology is often the organizer or conceptual initiator of actions that promote physical activity, movement and health. Through the work of its teaching staff, it has helped launch other kinesiology faculties in the Republic of Croatia and some in the region.
Vision
As the leading higher education institution in kinesiology in the region, the Faculty of Kinesiology at the
University of Zagreb aims to become integrated and competitive in the European higher education and research area and to create new and improve existing knowledge transfer systems in all fields of applied kinesiology.

Mission
The Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Zagreb is a leading higher education institution in the field of
kinesiology in the region educating staff in all areas of applied kinesiology based on the latest scientific and
professional knowledge. The Faculty of Kinesiology bases its work on high academic and ethical values,
knowledge based on research and expertise, and optimal infrastructure conditions. The Faculty of Kinesiology contributes significantly to the promotion of sports, physical recreation, physical and health education of pupils and students, as well as the quality of active life and health of Croatian citizens.
Strategic goals are aimed at quality advancement of the teaching process, ensuring the conditions for creative scientific research work aimed at creating new and deepening existing knowledge in all fields of general and applied kinesiology, and better positioning of the Faculty in the international academic community.

entityDescription:
SensFish is developing a smart, scenario-based and comprehensive technology to monitor the ocean. We are the crosssection of the sectors of space and ocean, disrupting the value chain of the global sustainable fishing industry.
 
The scalable solution leverages multi-modal data with AI and ML to enhance understanding of the fish population sizes by species and predict those trends and movements.
 
While functioning as SaaS, the technology factors in multi-modal sources of data through related applications for verification of ocean sustainability and big ‘ocean players' impact mitigation.
For example, the fusion of satellite fishing vessel tracking data and ocean protective measures attend to scenarios like illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, ocean pollution and seabed damage, through real-time alerts and risk scores, through parameters like marine protected areas (MPAs), vessel gear types, fishing concentration, effort and other.
 
Followed by the integration of satellite Earth Observation (EO) data on ocean conditions, such as salinity and temperature, combined with satellite tracking of warm-blooded marine mammals, carbon flux measurements between fish and sea sediments, and fish population statistics, provides valuable proxies for estimating fish population sizes. This approach also considers the impacts of climate change, including shifts in fish habitats to new locations, increased mortality rates, altered life cycles, and other ecological changes.
 
Seafood processors, on one hand, gain the ability to automate operations aligned with sustainability goals, ensuring compliance with ocean regulations and reporting requirements. This leads to improved efficiency, increased profitability, and greater consumer satisfaction with sustainable seafood products. On the other hand, regulatory bodies and agencies benefit from consistent ocean insights and predictive data, enabling enhanced fisheries management, informed decision-making, and support for decarbonization initiatives.
 
As a transformative solution for the future, aligned with the goals of achieving net zero emissions, sustainability, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), this vision encompasses the future of food security, ocean biodiversity, and the well-being of societies and fishing communities. These objectives converge to drive a rejuvenated and resilient economy, benefiting all stakeholders.

Such a network would represent the basis to serve an existing market of C6.7B and facilitate novel applications benefiting humanity such as early tsunami warning systems, crustal deformation monitoring and space weather monitoring, on a more larger and more accurate scale than previously possible.

onocoy incentivizes the transparent construction of such a network in a decentralized way with blockchain-based tokens, open standards and hardware, and participatory governance that includes all stakeholders of the ecosystem including existing competing actors and users of their services. description:
4D Fusion sp. z o.o. is a Polish deep-tech SME focused on advanced additive manufacturing and functional materials. The company was founded in 2024 and has been organically developed since then through collaboration with Polish academia on new functional materials and processes. 4D Fusion commercialises a new class of 4D printing technology that enables rapid development and industrialisation of polymer-based composites and smart structures, from laboratory concepts through functional demonstrators to scalable series production and technology transfer to customers’ lines.

Our mission is to provide a "materials technology sandbox" – an integrated ecosystem of hardware, materials and services that allows engineers and scientists to design, prototype, validate and scale up production of new materials and devices, from gram-scale R&D batches to mass-manufacturing, with very short iteration cycles and minimal material consumption.

The company is based in Poland and builds on more than 20 years of experience of the founders in polymer processing, additive manufacturing, special-purpose systems and technology commercialisation. 4D Fusion already collaborates with leading Polish universities and institutes (e.g. AGH University of Krakow, Silesian University of Technology, Military University of Technology, Lukasiewicz – Institute of Non-Ferrous Metals, Institute of Physical Chemistry Polish Academy of Science).

Core technology – 4D Fusion Additive Manufacturing System

4D Fusion develops and supplies a proprietary multi-material additive manufacturing platform that combines classic FDM with a new extrusion head called BFG on a common motion system. The core system consists of the 4D Fusion BFG head, a patented extrusion module with a modular plastification system and actively controlled thermal zones; dual FDM modules (1.75 mm and 2.85 mm) for structural polymers and standard engineering materials; and a unified motion and control system that enables the combination of multiple deposition modes in a single build and can be customised and extended with quality-assurance and process options (e.g. heated build chamber, vision/QC, additional process sensors). The BFG head can use virtually any thermoplastic polymer as a base matrix, achieve very high loading of functional additives (metals, ceramics, magnetic powders, bio-fillers, regolith simulants) up to ~70–80% vol., maintain precise formulation control with minimal need for processing aids, print shear-sensitive or temperature-sensitive additives and produce material inserts with minimal use of heat, water and feedstock.

The BFG head supports several deposition techniques in one platform, including classical 2.5D/3D printing (layer-by-layer), pouring and over-moulding into cavities, foaming for lightweight cellular structures, smearing for thin functional layers and interfaces, sedimentation for graded structures with controlled particle distribution, and matrix extrusion through shaped dies.

This architecture allows users to develop and print advanced multi-material parts that combine structural, sensing, magnetic, shielding or bio-functional roles in a single component.

Heritage and TRL 
The present 4D Fusion AM System is in advanced industrial stage, with first units planned for delivery to research and industrial customers. The technology has been validated with multiple material families, including highly filled composites, magnetic materials, regolith-polymer blends and bio-related formulations. 
Space-related capabilities and use cases
4D Fusion technology is particularly relevant for ESA activities in advanced manufacturing, ISRU and future habitats, where flexible use of local resources and complex functional materials is required.
Key space-related capabilities: 4D Fusion can process regolith-based and regolith-polymer composite materials and work with polymers that are normally not printable (e.g. PVC-based or highly doped matrices). The platform enables rapid screening of new formulations with gram-scale feedstock quantities, production of functionally graded materials with controlled changes in filler content or type, and direct integration of sensing, shielding, magnetic or antimicrobial functions into printed parts. Together with ESA and industrial partners, 4D Fusion can co-develop and validate new functional materials for mechanisms and satellite structures.
Illustrative applications under discussion or exploration: potential use cases include structural and non-structural components for surface habitats and infrastructure based on regolith-polymer composites, radiation and particle shielding elements combining polymer matrices with high-Z or magnetic fillers, embedded ion, pH or chemical sensors and smart inserts for environmental monitoring, lightweight magnetic components and mechanisms produced with highly filled elastomer matrices, as well as hybrid armour and functional protection systems using gradient or multi-layer composites.
The system is designed with in-situ operations in mind: compact form factor, modular process chain, and a clean, gram-scale material insert concept that can be coupled with an automated material preparation unit.
Products and services
4D Fusion offers an integrated portfolio of products and services. The 4D Fusion AM System is a modular multi-material printer with BFG + FDM, tailored to R&D labs, industrial innovation centres and space-related testbeds. The company develops and supplies gram-scale material inserts for specific polymers and composites, both from an open catalogue and as customer-specific or licensed materials. In addition, 4D Fusion provides R&D and engineering services covering formulation of new polymer composites and smart materials, design and fabrication of demonstrators, samples and functional prototypes, as well as participation in joint EU, ESA and national research projects where it delivers the AM platform, material know-how and process development.
Why 4D Fusion is relevant for ESA stakeholders
For ESA stakeholders, 4D Fusion offers a single platform to explore structural, electrical, magnetic, shielding and sensor functions within one printed component, providing true multi-material and multi-physics capability. Technology delivers high information density per kilogram of material, enabling many iterations and variants from very limited feedstock, which is particularly important when working with scarce or expensive materials and simulants. The technology is aligned with ISRU strategies through its ability to incorporate and characterise local granular resources such as regolith, recycled polymers and bio-derived fillers in robust polymer matrices. Because the same platform can be used in academic research, industrial R&D and early pilot production, it helps bridge the gap between science and industry and accelerates the transfer of novel materials into real applications.
4D Fusion is interested in partnering with ESA directorates, primes and research institutions on on-ground technology maturation for in-situ manufacturing and ISRU, advanced polymer and composite materials for space systems, and the development of functional demonstrators for habitats, robotics, sensors and protection systems.

entityDescription:
The National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics - NIEP is the successor of research institutions that aimed to study earthquakes.
In 1895, the first seismic station in Romania was established, within the Meteorological Institute of Bucharest.
The institutions that dealt with research in the field of Earth physics were, in order: the Center for Geophysical Research (CCG) of the Romanian Academy (1961-1970), followed by the Institute of Applied Geophysics (1970-1974) and the Institute of Geology and Geophysics (IGG, 1974-1977), both belonging to the Ministry of Mines, Petroleum and Geology.
In February 1977, the Center for Earth Physics (CFP) was established by merging the Department of Seismology within the Institute of Geology and Geophysics of Romania with the Geodynamics laboratory within the Romanian Academy.
In 1994 the Center for Earth Physics (CFP) was transformed into the National Institute for Earth Physics - NIEP, and in 1996, it became the National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics - NIEP.

Structure The National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics carries out scientific research and technological development activities in the field of Earth Physics, in general, and seismology in particular.

CEEIARAGON is a Business Innovation Centre founded in 1992 to promote the creation, growth, and scale-up of innovative companies in Aragon (Northeast of Spain). This EU|BIC, supported mainly by the Regional Government of Aragon in partnership with regional stakeholders such as business organisations, trade unions, the Chamber of Commerce, and the University of Zaragoza, covers an area of 48,000 km².

We operate across the three provinces of Aragon—Zaragoza, Huesca, and Teruel—**offering 7,000 m² of incubation space and a comprehensive range of support services that accompany companies from early-stage ideation to scale-up and consolidation. We offer incubation space in the three capitals, Zaragoza, Huesca and Teruel. 
We have more than 33 years of experience incubating and scaling technology-based projects, including aerospace projects. The aerospace cluster is located in our Zaragoza incubator since its foundation.
CEEIARAGON is an active member of several networks. In addition to being part of the European Business and Innovation Centres Network -EBN-, we are members of ANCES (the Spanish association of BICs), Red ARCE (the Aragonese network of entrepreneurship support centres), and the PI+D+I network (R&D+I network) led by the Centre for the Development of Industrial Technology (CDTI), a public entity fostering innovation in Spanish companies. We are open to collaborating with any network that helps us and our clients grow, cooperate, and learn.
We remain faithful to our traditional role as a BIC/CEEI, while continuously evolving and adapting to new methodologies and innovation models. entityName: Technical University of Sofia -  - Faculty of Transport
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Transport is an educational and research structure at the Technical University of Sofia. It educates specialists who can design, operate and service various types of transport vehicles in the field of land, air and space transport. The Faculty has specialists who can solve tasks related to problems in aviation and space technology. It has a modern material and technical base for simulation and experimental /real-life/ studies of specific characteristics of various types of objects intended for use in aviation and space technology. The faculty has laboratories for:
1) Vibroacoustic tests
2) Aerodynamic tests
3) Thermal tests
4) Clean room for assembly and testing of CubeSat satellites
The laboratories can perform some of the mandatory tests required for the flight of CubeSat and other satellites, such as:
1. Vibration Test: Sine and Random
2. Acoustic Test
3. Thermal Cycling test
4. Functional Test / Power-On Test
5. EMC/EMI Test
6. Fit Check
7. Subsystem tests /EPS Test, ADCS Test, Payload Test/
